films.title: American Folklore
films.description: Adam Crew and Fred Zahina's 32-minute Toebock road film follows a loose family of West Coast skateboarders from Northern California through Oregon to Washington's Kitsap County. Six named sections anchor a broader scene roster as the crew travels through Santa Rosa, Bodega Bay, Bremerton and the Olympic Peninsula.
creditNotes: Toebock's official upload supplies six timestamped named sections and credits Adam Crew and Fred Zahina with the film, Adam Crew as editor, Colton Light, Ben Ericson and Drew Cercley with additional video, Fred Zahina with Super 8, Ben Erickson with 16mm and Neil Hager with the main title.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies the release as a 32-minute 2026 full-length and indexes 16 named people plus the collective Foley Street section; its soundtrack detail supports four further named appearances.

The source spells Ben's surname both Ericson and Erickson in separate credit roles; both source spellings are preserved rather than silently conflated. No unsupported formal director credit is asserted.
locations: San Francisco Bay Area, California, USA
films.locationNote: The official project page describes the route from Northern California's Bay Area through Oregon to Kitsap County and identifies Santa Rosa, Bodega Bay, Bremerton and Olympic Peninsula imagery; no more specific itinerary is asserted.
films.historicalContext: American Folklore is Toebock's final chapter in a long-running Pacific Northwest filmography and preserves Adam Crew's last skateboarding clips. It premiered in theaters and clubs for roughly six months before its February 2026 online release.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It is dedicated black-and-white road-film artwork with a skater beside the Toebock van, a West Coast map and large yellow AMERICAN FOLKLORE title treatment.

First-party project page identifies the film by Fred Zahina and Adam Crew, the featured principals and the West Coast route, and links the same exact complete-film player and physical release.

Independent filmography classifies American Folklore as a 32-minute 2026 full-length, preserves the timestamped structure, indexes 16 named people plus the Foley Street collective and corroborates the production credits.
Contemporary independent coverage documents the online release, six-month premiere run, 32-minute runtime, Adam Crew's final clips and the supported camera, film-format, title and editing credits.

films.title: FORGHETABOUTIT
films.description: Dustin Dollin's 28-minute Piss Drunx full-length cuts six street parts through a deliberately chaotic mix of formats and frame rates. Matisse Banc, Enzo Morel, Maite Steenhoudt, Jamie Tancowny, Jeroen Bruggeman and Alexey Krasniy carry the film from its opening section through the 22-minute outro.
creditNotes: Free Skate Magazine's own upload supplies all six timestamped parts and explicitly credits Dustin Dollin as editor.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies the release as a 28-minute full-length, matches all six riders and preserves nine additional production contributors without assigning unsupported formal roles.
Free Skate Magazine's release article identifies the project as a Dustin Dollin production and a PD Skateboards full-length.
locations: New York City, New York, USA
films.locationNote: Free Skate Magazine specifically describes Alexey Krasniy's section as spanning Barcelona to New York City; no broader film-wide itinerary is asserted.
films.historicalContext: FORGHETABOUTIT extends the Piss Drunx film lineage with a new multinational crew and Dollin's deliberately rough, multi-format editing style, pairing established names with emerging street talent.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube max-resolution thumbnail was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It is a clean full-frame skate still from the film with no trailer, episode or compilation labeling; the title and full-length context are supplied by the upload and release article.
